title: Conditional values
simpler: The value that the condition reads is also owned and changed in CSS. There is no class to toggle from a script, and when() accepts comparisons such as --count > 3.
differences: Native if() tests style(), media() and supports() queries. when() tests Reactive CSS state, comparisons and logical operators.
With native if(), something still has to change --theme: a class, an attribute or a script.
Conditions made only of boolean states compile to native if() where the browser supports it. This one compares a keyword, so it runs in the runtime.
An unknown when() condition gives no value. A native if() with no matching branch and no else is invalid at computed-value time.
If a condition depends only on a media query, keep it native: if(media(…)) or @media.
Native if() is not available in every browser yet. Check support before relying on it.
